_about: Spring-bone chain spec for Whale-chan (chibi whale-girl maid), consumed by hookup_whalechan.py,
which resolves every 'frac' box into the absolute world-space 'bbox' that build_vrm.py understands.
Numbers come from tools/vrm/measure_turnaround.py over spikes/model/turnaround/{front,right,back}.png
(see tools/vrm/evidence/turnaround_landmarks.json and REPORT_hookup.md for the derivation).
frac axes, all in fractions of the model HEIGHT (H) after --height normalisation:
x     from the hips bone (the symmetry centre); + = character's left (Blender +X after a glTF import)
depth from the front-most plane of the bbox, backwards (0 = face / skirt front, 0.77 = tail tip)
z     from the bbox bottom (0 = sole, 1 = ahoge tip)
Height is the only bbox measure that survives the T-pose bake (width grows from 0.59 H in the
35-degree A-pose to about 0.76 H in T-pose) and a curled-vs-straight tail (depth 0.77 H straight,
about 0.55 H curled), so nothing here is a fraction of width or depth.
x is measured from the HIPS bone (bbox centre only if the rig has no hips) - an asymmetric or
raised arm skews the bbox centre; the front plane is the bbox min y, the floor the bbox min z.
prefer: if the GLB has a mesh whose name matches 'object', that mesh is the part (no bbox);
else if a material name matches 'material', the selector is material AND bbox (frac_material
when given - a wider box that is safe once the material excludes skin/arms); else bbox only.
Chains are applied in order and later chains re-claim overlapping vertices, so the hair strands
come after the skirt/tail and the ears after the side locks.
Reference proportions (from the turnaround): head 0.62-0.93 H, eyes 0.69 H, shoulders 0.56 H,
waist 0.47 H, skirt 0.20-0.45 H, hips 0.32 H, tail exits the skirt at 0.19 H and its flukes span
0.15-0.36 H, arm length 0.24 H, upper-body half width 0.26 H.

chains.name: tail
chains._why: root at the lower back under the skirt (hips at 0.32 H, exit at 0.19 H); the tail is the only thing behind the skirt back (0.37 H) below 0.37 H; x is wide because the flukes curl to one side in the front/back views (fluke centre at +-0.30 H)

chains.name: skirt_front
chains._why: apron/skirt front between the hem (0.20 H) and the waist band (0.45 H); depth stops before the legs' front plane (0.12 H) so the socks stay on the leg bones

chains.name: skirt_back
chains._why: skirt back panel + bow (depth 0.25-0.39 H, the skirt back edge is at 0.37 H); ends before the tail box starts at 0.40 H

chains.name: hair_back_L
chains._why: left half of the back hair: behind the upper back (0.32 H) out to the hair's back edge (0.54 H), from the headdress (0.88 H) down to 0.36 H; the last 0.12 H of tips (down to 0.24 H) are left to the skirt/tail boxes on purpose

chains.name: sidelock_L
chains._why: left side lock beside the head (x 0.12-0.30 H, depth 0.16-0.26 H). bbox-only fallback stops at 0.60 H because a T-posed upper arm crosses z 0.50-0.58 H in the same x range; with a hair material the box runs down to the hand level (0.36 H)

chains.name: bangs
chains._why: front bangs on the forehead: from the brow line (0.72 H) to under the headdress (0.88 H), front 0.16 H of the head; the forehead skin under them (hidden) moves with them

chains.name: ear_L
chains._why: left fin ear: root at x 0.20 H, tip at 0.30 H, z 0.65-0.72 H, mid-depth of the head (0.24-0.41 H); listed after the side locks so the ear wins the overlap

chains.name: ahoge
chains._why: the curl on top: everything above the headdress top (0.93 H), within 0.08 H of the centre line, on the front half of the skull (depth 0.05-0.25 H)
